newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai police detain "serial killer" suspect.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai police detain "serial killer" suspect.

text.p: Shanghai police have detained a man in connection with a series of murders and robberies which have terrorised the city in recent weeks, the official media reported on Thursday.
A radio announcement said police picked up a 26-year-old man on Wednesday during an investigation into 13 robberies in which two women were killed.

"Since mid-March there have been 13 cases of murder and robbery of women in the Yangpu and Baoshan districts of Shanghai, causing two deaths and 12 injuries to innocent people," the radio announcement said.
The killer targeted middle-aged women and used an iron bar or other blunt instrument in the attacks, the announcement said.

It was the first mention in the official media of the case, which has spurred increasingly lurid talk around China's biggest city in the past week of up to 20 deaths or more, including some in the Baoshan area.
The rumours variously said the killer was targeting young women with long hair, that he used a hammer to kill his victims and that he would continue until he had murdered 100 women.
A 42-year-old truck driver was executed in the southern Chinese province on Guangdong in 1995 after being found guilty of murdering 12 young women between 1990 and 1994.
